newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares end down as electronic trade starts.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares end down as electronic trade starts.

text.p: Most blue chips lost slightly by Monday's close, with higher volume but trading delays as new electronic trading methods were introduced.

RTF was the lone riser to 1.25 lats from 1.23 lats as it traded 1,500 lats of shares. The delays came as the bourse ironed out hitches from the introduction of an electronic order system. Previously brokers had to go to the bourse to place orders.
Olainfarm, a secondary list newcomer, had its price set at higher than expected at 2.45 lats on volume of 26,100 lats.
The market forecasts earlier ranged between 70 santimes to 1.50 lats per share.
"The price was unexpectedly high and in the coming two weeks I would expect it to come down," said one trader.
Total turnover came to 80,000 lats from 35,000 lats and the Rietumu index finished 0.12 percent lower at 153.93.
Valmiera Glassfibre and Unibanka remained stable. Valmiera closed at 1.50 lats and traded 15,000 lats of shares while Unibanka stayed put at 3.40 on volume of 4,500 lats.
Elsewhere on the official list, Riga Shipyard edged down one santime to 1.36 lats on 8,200 lats and Staburadze confectionery was also one santime down to 2.69 lats on 6,000 lats.
Kaija fish cannery slipped two santimes to 2.17 lats as it saw 3,500 lats of shares change hands.
Daugavpils Chain, a secondary list stock, lost four santimes to 1.16 lats on trade of 6,900 lats.
